newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU politicians cast doubt on Turkish membership.
newsitem.headline: EU politicians cast doubt on Turkish membership.

text.p: European centrist political leaders said on Tuesday they would not submit to blackmail from Turkey over European Union enlargement and cast serious doubt over the likelihood of Turkey joining the EU soon.

"Regarding Turkish membership in the EU, everybody is clearly very hesitant," Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker told reporters during a break in a meeting of the mainly Christian Democrat European People's Party.
Portuguese opposition leader Marcelo Reblo de Sousa criticised suggestions that Turkey would veto enlargement of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation if it is kept out of the 15-member EU.
"One idea that dominated this meeting was a commitment not to accept blackmail whatsoever," he told Portuguese reporters.

He said the political leaders had doubts about Turkey's commitment to human rights. "Human rights are very far from being respected in Turkey," he said. "It doesn't make sense to accept a country that doesn't respect them."

Despite the wariness about full membership, Juncker said the EU should have a special relationship with Turkey and should provide various aid packages that have been promised to Ankara. The aid has been blocked by the European Parliament because of human rights concerns.

Turkey signed an association agreement with what is now the European Union in 1963 and formally applied to join the bloc in 1987. The Commission ruled that Turkey was not ready on both economic and democratic grounds.
Since then, a stream of central and eastern European countries have been promised eventual EU membership, and Turkey has put pressure on the EU to accept its own application.
